tagline: Up the San Ramon Valley under Mount Diablo.
intro: From the Alameda County line Interstate 680 runs north up the San Ramon Valley along the line of the Calaveras Fault, through San Ramon, Danville and Alamo to the Highway 24 junction at Walnut Creek. The valley narrows at Danville, between Las Trampas Ridge on the west and the Diablo Range on the east, with Mount Diablo standing up behind the town.

Danville farmed wheat first, then fruit and nuts once the Southern Pacific ran a spur line through in 1891. The freeway cut through Danville in the mid-1960s, and an old railroad line through town is now the Iron Horse Regional Trail.

moments.title: Danville
moments.text: The 1891 Southern Pacific depot now holds the Museum of the San Ramon Valley, and the Danville Hotel, moved in 1927 to face Hartz Avenue, still stands downtown.

moments.title: Tao House
moments.text: Eugene O'Neill spent his Nobel Prize money on a house in the hills above Danville and wrote The Iceman Cometh and Long Day's Journey Into Night there between 1937 and 1944.

moments.title: Alamo
moments.text: In 1847 John Jones stopped his wagon here to ask Mary Ann whether she had ever seen anything so beautiful, and she wrote of wild oats waist high, rippling like a lake.

sources.label: Wikipedia, Eugene O'Neill National Historic Site
